name: Burning Steppes
summary: At Blackrock Mountain’s southern base, fire and lava have scorched the Burning Steppes. The land holds the main overland passage between Stormwind and Khaz Modan, where hostile clans and dragons threaten travelers.

sections.title: A Cataclysmic Origin
sections.body:
The Burning Steppes were once the northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains. Centuries ago, during the War of the Three Hammers, the exiled Dark Iron clan built Thaurissan as its capital here. Facing defeat by the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan tried to summon elemental forces.

His spell shattered the surrounding mountains and brought Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. Rivers of lava opened, and Blackrock Mountain rose from the earth. The blast left the steppes charred and barren.

sections.title: Echoes of the Second War
sections.body:
During the Second War, Blackrock Spire became the Old Horde’s foremost seat of power. Near the war’s end, the Grand Alliance of Lordaeron marched into the Burning Steppes and laid siege to the mountain. At its foot, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer struck down Lord Anduin Lothar.

Lothar’s death spurred the Allied armies to rout the orcs and win the war. Ash and rusted steel still mark the valley where the battle was fought.

sections.title: A Den of Monsters and Dragons
sections.body:
Blackrock orcs remain in the steppes, keeping the Old Horde’s cruelty despite Thrall’s New Horde in distant Kalimdor. From Blackrock Stronghold, they ally with the black dragonflight and Firegut ogres. They honor no truce.

Dark Iron dwarves and elemental servitors haunt the fiery ruins. Black drakes and wyrmkin prey on travelers crossing between Stormwind and the northern kingdoms.

faq.q: Why is the ground charred and covered in lava?
aliases: why is blackrock mountain a volcano
faq.answer: Centuries ago, Dark Iron Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan tried to summon an elemental minion to save his clan from defeat in the War of the Three Hammers. His spell breached the Elemental Plane by mistake and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The blast tore open the earth, raised Blackrock Mountain, and scorched the northern Redridge Mountains.

faq.q: Do the orcs here belong to Thrall's Horde?
faq.answer: No. The Burning Steppes’ Blackrock orcs refuse to join Thrall’s New Horde. They honor no armistice with the Alliance and keep the savage, warmongering traditions of the First and Second Wars. They serve Blackrock Spire and the black dragonflight.

Near the end of the Second War, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer slew Anduin Lothar at the foot of Blackrock Mountain in the Burning Steppes. Lothar’s death drove his second-in-command, Turalyon, and the Alliance forces into a counterattack that broke the Horde’s lines.

faq.q: Where can the Alliance find shelter in the steppes?
faq.answer: Alliance soldiers and travelers take shelter at Morgan’s Vigil, an elevated outpost in the zone’s southeastern foothills. Marshal Maxwell commands it, watches the northern pass, and monitors enemy troop movements around the mountain.

faq.q: Where does the Horde stage operations here?
faq.answer: Horde adventurers report to Flame Crest, an elevated camp on the northeastern ridge. Its emissaries watch the rival Blackrock clan and maintain flight connections to the Badlands, the Swamp of Sorrows, Searing Gorge, and the Riverglades.

faq.q: What are the Ruins of Thaurissan?
aliases: what is the destroyed dwarf city
faq.answer: The Ruins of Thaurissan are what remains of the grand city the Dark Iron clan built after its exile from Ironforge. When Thane Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros, the elemental blast destroyed his capital and bound the survivors to the Firelord’s will.

angles.text: As an Alliance traveler, you enter a somber and dangerous frontier where Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar fell. Marshal Maxwell at Morgan’s Vigil seeks brave champions against threats pressing toward Redridge.
As a member of Thrall’s New Horde, you know Flame Crest watches the dangerous, unrepentant Blackrock clan with deep concern. Their warmongering stains the honor of orckind.
As a dwarf, you know the stones of the steppes mark the Dark Iron clan’s folly during the War of the Three Hammers. Their capital was shattered, and Ragnaros was summoned.

As a miner, you can find rare minerals in this volcanic land, including rich thorium and Dark Iron deposits. The steppes are among the few open-air regions on Azeroth where Dark Iron can be harvested.
